BBC, 25 Nov 2026 17:53 GMT

Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk

A couple with a buggy walks past Poundland in Weymouth dressed in winter clothes while a woman with a buggy walks the other way

Watch: Why has Poundland collapsed into administration?

Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business.

The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers.

Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached.

Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had \"no alternative but to take this decision\", but was making it with \"sincere sadness and intense regret\".

He said the US owners Gordon Brothers had removed \"all borrowing facilities and access to our bank accounts\" on 27 October, and adequate funds had not been released since then to keep the business solvent.

\"Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern,\" he added.

Kelvin Blake, pictured at a protest in Walsall, has worked for Poundland for 25 years

Kelvin Blake, 62, who has worked for the firm for 25 years, while his partner has been there 29 years, said he was feeling \"down, depressed\", and because of his age, feared he would not find a job elsewhere.

\"We didn't want it, but it's come so now we've just got to face it and see what the future holds.

\"My income's gone,\" he added. \"Obviously, we'll be working until we're told to leave.

Alix Partners, which has been appointed as administrator, said it would  look at \"all options\" for the business, \"including sales of the business and its assets, either in whole or part\".

\"We appreciate this is a deeply concerning time for all involved - customers, suppliers and, in particular, Poundland colleagues,\" they said.

Its owner Gordon Brothers has been criticised over how it handled a potential sale of Poundland, with accusations the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off the chain's 600 shops and stock piecemeal after running it into the ground.

Gordon Brothers, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied such claims.

On the funding question, Gordon Brothers said it had loaned the firm £85m over a year to help save it from insolvency.

But critical insiders have said it stands to make its loans back and more from the insolvency process.

Previously, Gordon Brothers netted millions from liquidating the stock of fashion retailer LK Bennett, and in insolvency fees.

Gordon Brothers said on Wednesday that despite the Poundland management bringing about a turnaround over the past year, the firm was \"still vulnerable\" to inflation and any downturn in sales or profit margin, and it had faced \"several years of instability\".

A spokesperson added the firm's \"thoughts are with Poundland colleagues\".

It said it had stepped in to take over the firm in 2025 when it was struggling, when \"no one else was willing to finance the business\".

One of the central stumbling blocks in negotiations to keep the business afloat was a shareholder loan Gordon Brothers inherited when it bought the business for less than £1 last year.

Gordon Brothers was owed £22.5m of that loan, while the previous owner Pepco was owed £7.5m.

Gordon Brothers rejected various offers to buy the business as a going concern with deals to pay off that loan.

Irish firm Martin Property Group offered to pay off £5m of the loan up front, and defer the rest of the payments to 2030. This was rejected.

Gordon Brothers also rejected a deal from the London-based Xyra group, which offered £12.5m up front but ran out of time to get a deal over the line.

A German investment firm, Zachert Private Equity, is also understood to have made a late offer, but that too was rejected.

The crisis at Poundland really came to a head over the past few weeks after Gordon Brothers restricted access to funds for day-to-day operations.

This meant that stock at the retailer was not being replenished at the necessary pace in the vital run-up to the festive period.

British people, particularly teens and young adults, are having less or no sex compared to past generations, but lots are watching porn and sexting, a major study suggests.

It is the first time The National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles' (Natsal) research into general public sex lives has asked about online behaviours.

The latest results were published in The Lancet and were based on a survey of 6,700 people aged 16–59 who were selected at random across Britain.

Energy bills will rise by 26% for millions of households in January, the highest rate in nearly four years, after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.

Isaac, a student at Durham University, said he had no choice but to keep the heating in his student house on 'constantly' due to poor insulation, and he was not looking forward to the price increase.

In the Autumn budget, the government announced a one-off payment of £100 for households in council bands A to D, 'half a weekly shop' according to Isaac.
